newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seizes plane of American who flew to Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seizes plane of American who flew to Cuba.

text.p: An American who flew to Cuba to deliver medicine to children without U.S. approval was detained on Monday when he returned home and his plane seized.

Millard Harmon, 71, of Delmar, New York, landed his Beechcraft 36 at Albany County Airport in the afternoon, where federal and local officials took him into custody and examined his log books after he returned from Cuba via the Bahamas.
Harmon admitted he dropped off $50,000 worth of medicine in Cuba last week and started the trip home in sections on Easter Sunday.

The independently wealthy pilot said in an interview that he had planned to drop off the $50,000 worth of asthma inhalators and penicillin to doctors in the Cayman Islands, but he had engine trouble and was forced to land in Havana.
"The good Lord does strange things to me," said Harmon, who said he worked for 18 months to get federal permission to travel to Cuba and deliver the medicine.

After two hours of questioning in Albany, Harmon, a retired administrator at the State University of New York, was released but his red, white and black 27-year-old plane called the Ten Romeo was confiscated by federal authorities.

According to Richard Will, port director for U.S. Customs, Harmon faces a $5,000 fine for failing to comply with custom reporting requirements because all U.S. aircraft leaving Cuba are required to stop in Miami.
Harmon also could face federal charges for his trip because of the U.S. economic embargo on Cuba.
